---- MODULE W4Od15m3p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Engines, MaxTerm, NoPledge

ASSUME NoPledge \notin Engines

Terms == 1..MaxTerm
Quorums == {Q \in SUBSET Engines : 2 * Cardinality(Q) > Cardinality(Engines)}

VARIABLES seen, pledge, notices, printed, silent

vars == <<seen, pledge, notices, printed, silent>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ seen \in [Engines -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ pledge \in [Engines -> [trm : 0..MaxTerm, backs : Engines \cup {NoPledge}]]
    /\ notices \subseteq [cand : Engines, trm : Terms]
    /\ printed \subseteq [cand : Engines, trm : Terms]
    /\ silent \subseteq Engines

\* The engines that have pledged their book to candidate c for session term t.
Backers(c, t) == {e \in Engines : pledge[e].trm = t /\ pledge[e].backs = c}

Init ==
    /\ seen = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
    /\ pledge = [e \in Engines |-> [trm |-> 0, backs |-> NoPledge]]
    /\ notices = {}
    /\ printed = {}
    /\ silent = {}

\* A responsive engine opens a campaign to run the uncrossing for a fresh
\* session term.  Notices sit in an unordered pool, so peers may observe
\* campaigns in any order and may still see a superseded one afterwards.
Campaign(c, t) ==
    /\ c \notin silent
    /\ t > seen[c]
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![c] = t]
    /\ notices' = notices \cup {[cand |-> c, trm |-> t]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pledge, printed, silent>>

\* Pledging is one-shot for the whole opening session: an engine hands its
\* order book to exactly one campaign and can never hand it to another.  A
\* notice from a term the engine has already left is discarded as stale.
Pledge(e, n) ==
    /\ e \notin silent
    /\ n \in notices
    /\ pledge[e].trm = 0
    /\ n.trm >= seen[e]
    /\ pledge' = [pledge EXCEPT ![e] = [trm |-> n.trm, backs |-> n.cand]]
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![e] = n.trm]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<notices, printed, silent>>

\* Publishing the opening print is irreversible: it fixes the reference price
\* the whole session settles against, so it demands a pledged quorum.
Publish(c, t) ==
    /\ c \notin silent
    /\ Backers(c, t) \in Quorums
    /\ printed' = printed \cup {[cand |-> c, trm |-> t]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, pledge, notices, silent>>

\* Failover: an engine drops off the session floor without warning.  At least
\* two engines must stay up, so a campaign is still in principle winnable.
GoSilent(e) ==
    /\ e \notin silent
    /\ Cardinality(silent) + 2 < Cardinality(Engines)
    /\ silent' = silent \cup {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, pledge, notices, printed>>

\* A recovered engine is readmitted to the floor.  It keeps whatever pledge it
\* had already spent, so recovery never buys it a second pledge.
Rejoin(e) ==
    /\ e \in silent
    /\ silent' = silent \ {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, pledge, notices, printed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Engines, t \in Terms : Campaign(c, t) \/ Publish(c, t)
    \/ \E e \in Engines, n \in notices : Pledge(e, n)
    \/ \E e \in Engines : GoSilent(e) \/ Rejoin(e)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every engine spends its single pledge on one campaign, so two campaigns can
\* never both hold a quorum -- the opening print is fixed at most once.
OpeningPrintUnique == \A p, q \in printed : p.cand = q.cand /\ p.trm = q.trm

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Engines = {engAlpha, engBeta, engGamma}
    MaxTerm = 2
    NoPledge = nilPledge

INVARIANT OpeningPrintUnique
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction on a small set of matching engines. Before continuous trading begins, one engine must be chosen to run the uncrossing and publish the opening print -- the single reference price that every order in the auction settles against. Once that print is published it is irreversible: it has already been disseminated to the tape and to every clearing member, so a second print with a different price would mean two contradictory official openings for the same session.

The engines choose a runner by campaigning. A responsive engine opens a campaign for a session term strictly higher than any term it has itself observed, and the campaign notice joins an unordered pool that the other engines drain at their own pace. Because the pool is unordered, an engine may observe campaigns out of order and may still be handed a notice from a term that has already been superseded; it discards any notice whose term is older than the newest term it has seen.

An engine responds to a surviving notice by pledging its order book to that campaign. The pledge is one-shot for the whole opening session: an engine that has pledged its book to one campaign cannot pledge it again, to that campaign or any other, for the remainder of the session. A campaigner may publish the opening print only once a strict majority of engines have pledged their books to it under its own session term.

Engines can fail over. An engine may go silent at any moment without warning, and the remaining engines carry on campaigning; the session keeps at least two engines up so that a campaign remains winnable in principle. A recovered engine can be readmitted to the floor at any time, but it comes back carrying whatever pledge it had already spent, so recovering never buys an engine a second pledge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Because each engine spends its single session pledge on exactly one campaign, no two campaigns can both hold a majority of pledges, so every opening print that reaches the tape names the same runner and the same session term.

---- MODULE W4Od3m4p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, QueueCap, BatchSize, NoBank

ASSUME NoBank \notin Banks

VARIABLES stage, admitted, engine, posted, pushedBack

vars == <<stage, admitted, engine, posted, pushedBack>>

Typing ==
    /\ stage \in [Banks -> {"idle", "queued", "posting", "settled"}]
    /\ admitted \in Seq(Banks)
    /\ engine \in Banks \cup {NoBank}
    /\ posted \in [Banks -> 0..BatchSize]
    /\ pushedBack \subseteq Banks

Init ==
    /\ stage = [b \in Banks |-> "idle"]
    /\ admitted = <<>>
    /\ engine = NoBank
    /\ posted = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ pushedBack = {}

\* A bank offers its settlement batch to the admission queue.  The queue is
\* bounded, so the offer only lands while there is room in it.
Offer(b) ==
    /\ stage[b] = "idle"
    /\ b \notin pushedBack
    /\ Len(admitted) < QueueCap
    /\ admitted' = Append(admitted, b)
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<engine, posted, pushedBack>>

\* Backpressure: with the queue full the offer is refused outright and the
\* bank is told to come back later rather than being buffered somewhere else.
Refuse(b) ==
    /\ stage[b] = "idle"
    /\ b \notin pushedBack
    /\ Len(admitted) = QueueCap
    /\ pushedBack' = pushedBack \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, admitted, engine, posted>>

Relent(b) ==
    /\ b \in pushedBack
    /\ pushedBack' = pushedBack \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, admitted, engine, posted>>

\* The posting engine takes the bank at the head of the queue, and only when
\* it is standing free.
Admit ==
    /\ engine = NoBank
    /\ Len(admitted) > 0
    /\ engine' = Head(admitted)
    /\ admitted' = Tail(admitted)
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![Head(admitted)] = "posting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posted, pushedBack>>

\* Banks are slow but never fail: a bank may take many steps to walk its batch
\* through the engine, and the engine stays occupied for all of them.
PostLeg(b) ==
    /\ engine = b
    /\ posted[b] < BatchSize
    /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![b] = posted[b] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, admitted, engine, pushedBack>>

Withdraw(b) ==
    /\ engine = b
    /\ posted[b] = BatchSize
    /\ engine' = NoBank
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "settled"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, posted, pushedBack>>

Recycle(b) ==
    /\ stage[b] = "settled"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
    /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, engine, pushedBack>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Offer(b) \/ Refuse(b) \/ Relent(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : PostLeg(b) \/ Withdraw(b) \/ Recycle(b)
    \/ Admit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Two banks can never be walking their batches through the posting engine at
\* the same moment, however slow either of them is.
SettlementExclusion ==
    \A v, w \in Banks :
        (stage[v] = "posting" /\ stage[w] = "posting") => v = w

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {bkNorth, bkSouth, bkWest}
    QueueCap = 2
    BatchSize = 2
    NoBank = nilBank

INVARIANT SettlementExclusion
nl:
A national bank runs its interbank settlement in batches. Member banks bring a batch of payment legs to a single posting engine, and the engine is the critical resource: while one bank is walking its batch through, no other bank may touch it, because the engine rewrites the same set of reserve accounts leg by leg and interleaving two batches would post legs against balances that the other batch has already moved.

Access is arranged through a bounded admission queue. An idle bank offers its batch and is placed at the back of the queue, but only while the queue has room. When the queue is full the offer is refused outright rather than buffered somewhere else -- that is the backpressure -- and the refused bank is told to come back later. A bank that has been pushed back stays out of the queue until it relents and is allowed to offer again.

The posting engine takes the bank at the head of the queue, and only while it is standing free. Banks here are slow but never fail: once admitted, a bank posts its batch one leg at a time and may take many steps to finish, and the engine stays occupied for every one of them. Only when the bank has posted its whole batch does it withdraw and leave the engine free for the next bank in the queue. A bank that has settled can later recycle back to idle with a fresh batch and rejoin the queue.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two member banks are ever walking their batches through the posting engine at the same moment, however many legs either of them still has to post.

---- MODULE W4Od1m3p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, Supervisors, MaxTerm, NoSup, NoFlight

ASSUME NoSup \notin Supervisors /\ NoFlight \notin Flights

Terms == 1..MaxTerm

VARIABLES phase, holdStack, strip, claimed, chief

vars == <<phase, holdStack, strip, claimed, chief>>

Typing ==
    /\ phase \in [Flights -> {"parked", "holding", "rolling", "cleared"}]
    /\ holdStack \in Seq(Flights)
    /\ strip \in Flights \cup {NoFlight}
    /\ claimed \in [Supervisors -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ chief \in [sup : Supervisors \cup {NoSup}, trm : 0..MaxTerm]

Init ==
    /\ phase = [f \in Flights |-> "parked"]
    /\ holdStack = <<>>
    /\ strip = NoFlight
    /\ claimed = [s \in Supervisors |-> 0]
    /\ chief = [sup |-> NoSup, trm |-> 0]

\* A parked aircraft calls for departure and joins the hold in arrival order.
CallForDeparture(f) ==
    /\ phase[f] = "parked"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "holding"]
    /\ holdStack' = Append(holdStack, f)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<strip, claimed, chief>>

\* Failover in the tower: a supervisor claims a term newer than any yet
\* claimed.  Supervisors are slow but never fail, so the claim does not reach
\* the strip board in the same breath.
ClaimTerm(s, t) ==
    /\ \A d \in Supervisors : t > claimed[d]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![s] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, holdStack, strip, chief>>

TakeBoard(s) ==
    /\ claimed[s] > chief.trm
    /\ chief' = [sup |-> s, trm |-> claimed[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, holdStack, strip, claimed>>

\* Only the supervisor holding the strip board may release the runway, and
\* only while the strip is physically empty.
Release(s) ==
    /\ chief.sup = s
    /\ strip = NoFlight
    /\ Len(holdStack) > 0
    /\ strip' = Head(holdStack)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![Head(holdStack)] = "rolling"]
    /\ holdStack' = Tail(holdStack)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, chief>>

\* The aircraft rolls, gets airborne and hands the strip back.  A change of
\* supervisor part way through does not disturb an aircraft already rolling.
Airborne(f) ==
    /\ strip = f
    /\ phase[f] = "rolling"
    /\ strip' = NoFlight
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "cleared"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holdStack, claimed, chief>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A f \in Flights : phase[f] = "cleared"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights : CallForDeparture(f) \/ Airborne(f)
    \/ \E s \in Supervisors, t \in Terms : ClaimTerm(s, t)
    \/ \E s \in Supervisors : TakeBoard(s) \/ Release(s)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Supervisors, t \in Terms : ClaimTerm(s, t))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Supervisors : TakeBoard(s))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Supervisors : Release(s))
    /\ WF_vars(\E f \in Flights : Airborne(f))

\* However slowly the tower changes hands, two aircraft are never rolling on
\* the strip at the same moment.
StripExclusion ==
    \A f, g \in Flights :
        (phase[f] = "rolling" /\ phase[g] = "rolling") => f = g

EveryHoldEventuallyClears ==
    \A f \in Flights : (phase[f] = "holding") ~> (phase[f] = "cleared")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Flights = {fltAlpha, fltBravo}
    Supervisors = {supEast, supWest}
    MaxTerm = 2
    NoSup = nilSup
    NoFlight = nilFlight

INVARIANT StripExclusion
PROPERTY EveryHoldEventuallyClears
nl:
A regional airport allocates its single departure runway from the tower. A parked aircraft that wants to leave calls for departure and joins the hold, which the tower works in the order the calls arrived. The runway strip itself is the critical resource: only one aircraft may be rolling on it at a time, since a second aircraft released onto an occupied strip would be rolling towards a machine that has not yet lifted.

The tower is run by whichever supervisor currently holds the strip board, and the board changes hands by term. A supervisor may claim a term newer than any term yet claimed by anyone. Supervisors here are slow but they never fail: claiming a term does not put the claimant on the board in the same breath, so for a while the board is still held under the older term while a newer claim sits unheard. When the board does catch up, the supervisor with the newest claim takes it over.

Only the supervisor actually holding the board may release the runway, and only while the strip is physically empty. Releasing takes the aircraft at the front of the hold and sends it rolling. The aircraft then gets airborne and hands the strip back; a change of supervisor part way through does not disturb an aircraft that is already rolling, because the strip is a physical fact rather than a tower record. Once every aircraft has been cleared the tower falls quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two aircraft are ever rolling on the departure strip at the same moment, however often and however slowly the strip board changes hands.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every aircraft that calls for departure and joins the hold is eventually cleared into the air.

---- MODULE W4Od14m6p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, Horizon, LeaseTicks, Frames, NoDrone

ASSUME NoDrone \notin Drones

MinNat(a, b) == IF a < b THEN a ELSE b

VARIABLES clock, lease, mode, dark, backlog

vars == <<clock, lease, mode, dark, backlog>>

Typing ==
    /\ clock \in 0..Horizon
    /\ lease \in [holder : Drones \cup {NoDrone}, until : 0..Horizon]
    /\ mode \in [Drones -> {"idle", "seeking", "downlink"}]
    /\ dark \subseteq Drones
    /\ backlog \in [Drones -> 0..Frames]

\* A drone is actually putting energy on the uplink only if it believes it
\* holds the modem and has not gone dark.
Radiating(d) == mode[d] = "downlink" /\ d \notin dark

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ lease = [holder |-> NoDrone, until |-> 0]
    /\ mode = [d \in Drones |-> "idle"]
    /\ dark = {}
    /\ backlog = [d \in Drones |-> Frames]

Seek(d) ==
    /\ d \notin dark
    /\ mode[d] = "idle"
    /\ backlog[d] > 0
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "seeking"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, dark, backlog>>

\* The relay hands out the modem only once the standing lease is a full tick
\* past its expiry, which is exactly when the previous holder's own timer has
\* already fired and taken it off the air.
Grant(d) ==
    /\ d \notin dark
    /\ mode[d] = "seeking"
    /\ \/ lease.holder = NoDrone
       \/ lease.until < clock
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> d, until |-> MinNat(clock + LeaseTicks, Horizon)]
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "downlink"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, dark, backlog>>

SendFrame(d) ==
    /\ d \notin dark
    /\ mode[d] = "downlink"
    /\ lease.until > clock
    /\ backlog[d] > 0
    /\ backlog' = [backlog EXCEPT ![d] = backlog[d] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, mode, dark>>

Yield(d) ==
    /\ mode[d] = "downlink"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.holder = NoDrone]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, dark, backlog>>

\* One tick of the shared burn-over clock.  Every holder whose lease has run
\* out at the new time drops off the air on its own timer, dark or not.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ mode' = [d \in Drones |->
                  IF mode[d] = "downlink" /\ lease.until <= clock + 1
                  THEN "idle" ELSE mode[d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, dark, backlog>>

\* The relay reaps a lease that has run out, taking its holder off the air in
\* the same movement so the modem is never left doubly claimed.
Reap ==
    /\ lease.holder # NoDrone
    /\ lease.until <= clock
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![lease.holder] = "idle"]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.holder = NoDrone]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, dark, backlog>>

\* A drone back at idle picks up a fresh block of imagery to send.
Refill(d) ==
    /\ d \notin dark
    /\ mode[d] = "idle"
    /\ backlog[d] = 0
    /\ backlog' = [backlog EXCEPT ![d] = Frames]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, mode, dark>>

\* A single drone may be lost to the fire without ever saying so.
GoDark(d) ==
    /\ dark = {}
    /\ dark' = {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, mode, backlog>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Seek(d) \/ Grant(d) \/ SendFrame(d) \/ Yield(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Refill(d) \/ GoDark(d)
    \/ Tick \/ Reap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Two surviving drones never radiate on the incident downlink at once, even
\* across a lease that lapsed while its holder was still holding the modem.
DownlinkExclusion ==
    \A c, d \in Drones : (Radiating(c) /\ Radiating(d)) => c = d

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {drnScout, drnRidge, drnCanyon}
    Horizon = 3
    LeaseTicks = 2
    Frames = 1
    NoDrone = nilDrone

INVARIANT DownlinkExclusion
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm flies a fixed set of drones over an active burn. All of them share one narrowband uplink to the incident command relay, and that uplink is the critical resource: two drones radiating on it at the same moment jam each other and command loses the imagery from both.

The relay hands the modem out on a lease with an expiry. A drone with frames still to send announces itself as seeking, and the relay grants it the modem until a fixed number of ticks from now, clipped to the end of the burn-over window. The relay will only grant a modem when the standing lease is either unheld or a full tick past its expiry -- by that time the previous holder's own countdown timer has already fired and taken it off the air. Every tick of the shared clock, any holder whose lease has run out at the new time drops off the air on its own timer, whether or not it is still healthy.

The relay also reaps a lease that has run out, taking its holder off the air in the same movement, so an expired modem is never left doubly claimed. A drone holding a live lease sends its frames one at a time and may hand the modem back early. A drone that is back at idle with nothing left to send picks up a fresh block of imagery and starts seeking again. Drones over a fire can be lost: one drone in the swarm may go dark at any moment without ever announcing it, and a drone that has gone dark puts nothing on the air, though the relay has no way to tell the difference between a dark drone and a quiet one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two surviving drones ever radiate on the incident uplink at the same moment, including across a lease that lapsed while its holder still believed it held the modem.

---- MODULE W4Od14m4p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Reports, StageCap, MaxRev

VARIABLES sheet, rev, stance, basis, snapshot

vars == <<sheet, rev, stance, basis, snapshot>>

Typing ==
    /\ sheet \subseteq Reports
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ stance \in [Reports -> {"held", "staged", "merged", "bounced"}]
    /\ basis \in [Reports -> 0..MaxRev]
    /\ snapshot \in [Reports -> SUBSET Reports]

Staged == {r \in Reports : stance[r] = "staged"}

Init ==
    /\ sheet = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ stance = [r \in Reports |-> "held"]
    /\ basis = [r \in Reports |-> 0]
    /\ snapshot = [r \in Reports |-> {}]

\* An observer reads the common sheet and stages its report against the
\* revision it read.  The staging area is small, and when it is full no
\* further report can be staged -- that is the backpressure on the observers.
Stage(r) ==
    /\ stance[r] = "held"
    /\ Cardinality(Staged) < StageCap
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![r] = "staged"]
    /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![r] = rev]
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![r] = sheet]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, rev>>

\* Staged reports reach the sheet in whatever order the mesh delivers them,
\* not the order they were staged in.  A report writes back the whole sheet it
\* read plus itself, so it may only land while the revision it read is still
\* the standing one.
Merge(r) ==
    /\ stance[r] = "staged"
    /\ basis[r] = rev
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ sheet' = snapshot[r] \cup {r}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![r] = "merged"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<basis, snapshot>>

\* A report whose read is out of date is bounced rather than written back,
\* because writing it would put back a sheet that is missing whatever landed
\* in the meantime.
Bounce(r) ==
    /\ stance[r] = "staged"
    /\ basis[r] # rev
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![r] = "bounced"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, rev, basis, snapshot>>

Reread(r) ==
    /\ stance[r] = "bounced"
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![r] = "held"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, rev, basis, snapshot>>

Rest ==
    /\ \A r \in Reports : stance[r] = "merged"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reports : Stage(r) \/ Merge(r) \/ Bounce(r) \/ Reread(r)
    \/ Rest

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every report that has been merged is still on the common sheet: a later
\* write-back never carries away an observation that landed before it.
NoLostObservation == {r \in Reports : stance[r] = "merged"} \subseteq sheet

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Reports = {rptSmoke, rptFront, rptSpot}
    StageCap = 2
    MaxRev = 3

INVARIANT NoLostObservation
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm keeps one common situation sheet listing the observations the swarm has confirmed. Each drone contributes its own report to that sheet, but the mesh radio between the drones has no ordering guarantee at all: reports that were prepared in one order reach the sheet in whatever order the mesh happens to deliver them.

A drone contributes by first reading the sheet -- taking a copy of its contents and the revision number it carried -- and then staging its report against that read. The staging area is deliberately small: while it is full no further report can be staged, and the drones holding reports simply have to wait, which is the backpressure the mesh needs to stop the observers running ahead of the sheet.

A staged report writes back the whole sheet it read plus its own observation. Because the write-back is a whole-sheet write, it may only land while the revision the drone read is still the standing revision; landing bumps the revision. A staged report whose read has gone out of date is bounced instead of written back, since putting its copy back would carry away whatever landed in the meantime. A bounced drone re-reads the sheet and stages afresh. Once every report has been merged the swarm rests.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every report that has been merged is still on the common situation sheet, so no later write-back ever carries away an observation that landed before it.

---- MODULE W4Od18m5p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Hubs, Requests, MaxPolicy

Policies == 1..MaxPolicy
Quorums == {Q \in SUBSET Hubs : 2 * Cardinality(Q) > Cardinality(Hubs)}

VARIABLES policy, attest, verdict, mute

vars == <<policy, attest, verdict, mute>>

Typing ==
    /\ policy \in 0..MaxPolicy
    /\ attest \in [Requests -> [Hubs -> 0..MaxPolicy]]
    /\ verdict \in [Requests -> [state : {"open", "granted"}, under : 0..MaxPolicy]]
    /\ mute \subseteq Hubs

Backers(q, e) == {h \in Hubs : attest[q][h] >= e}

Init ==
    /\ policy = 1
    /\ attest = [q \in Requests |-> [h \in Hubs |-> 0]]
    /\ verdict = [q \in Requests |-> [state |-> "open", under |-> 0]]
    /\ mute = {}

\* The household rolls its access policy forward, for instance when a resident
\* is added or a key is revoked.  Attestations written under the old policy
\* are thereby made stale rather than being erased.
Rekey(e) ==
    /\ e > policy
    /\ policy' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attest, verdict, mute>>

\* A hub attests to a request under the policy it currently reads.  A hub that
\* has already attested under an older policy re-attests under the new one.
Attest(h, q) ==
    /\ h \notin mute
    /\ verdict[q].state = "open"
    /\ attest[q][h] < policy
    /\ attest' = [attest EXCEPT ![q][h] = policy]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<policy, verdict, mute>>

\* A request is carried out only on a quorum of attestations written under the
\* policy standing right now; attestations left over from a superseded policy
\* are not counted towards it.
Grant(q) ==
    /\ verdict[q].state = "open"
    /\ {h \in Hubs : attest[q][h] = policy} \in Quorums
    /\ verdict' = [verdict EXCEPT ![q] = [state |-> "granted", under |-> policy]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<policy, attest, mute>>

\* A single hub may drop off the mesh without announcing it.
GoMute(h) ==
    /\ mute = {}
    /\ mute' = {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<policy, attest, verdict>>

Settled ==
    /\ \A q \in Requests : verdict[q].state = "granted"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Policies : Rekey(e)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs, q \in Requests : Attest(h, q)
    \/ \E q \in Requests : Grant(q)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : GoMute(h)
    \/ Settled

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E h \in Hubs, q \in Requests : Attest(h, q))
    /\ WF_vars(\E q \in Requests : Grant(q))

\* Nothing is ever carried out on the strength of a superseded hub: every
\* granted request is backed by a quorum that attested under the policy the
\* grant was made against, or a newer one.
NoStaleAuthority ==
    \A q \in Requests :
        (verdict[q].state = "granted") => (Backers(q, verdict[q].under) \in Quorums)

EveryRequestEventuallySettled ==
    \A q \in Requests : (verdict[q].state = "open") ~> (verdict[q].state = "granted")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Hubs = {hubHall, hubKitchen, hubGarage}
    Requests = {reqFront, reqPatio}
    MaxPolicy = 2

INVARIANT NoStaleAuthority
PROPERTY EveryRequestEventuallySettled
nl:
A smart-home door lock network spreads its decisions across several hubs. No single hub may carry out an unlock request on its own: a request is carried out only when a strict majority of the hubs have attested to it.

The household's access policy rolls forward from time to time -- a resident is added, a lost key is revoked -- and each roll gives the policy a newer number. Attestations written under an older policy are not erased when the policy rolls; they simply become stale. A hub attests to an open request under the policy it currently reads, and a hub whose attestation was written under an older policy re-attests under the new one.

The rule that keeps a revoked resident from getting through is that a request is carried out only on a majority of attestations written under the policy standing at that moment. Attestations left over from a superseded policy do not count towards that majority, so a hub that has not caught up with the roll cannot contribute to letting anybody in. When a request is carried out, the network records which policy it was carried out under.

Hubs on a home mesh are not reliable. A single hub may drop off without announcing it and then attests to nothing further, while the remaining hubs carry on; because a majority of three is two, the network can still reach decisions with one hub gone. Once every request has been settled the network is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Nothing is ever carried out on the strength of a superseded hub -- every granted request is backed by a majority of hubs that attested under the policy the grant was made against, or under a newer one.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every open unlock request is eventually granted.

---- MODULE W4Od9m9p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, Load, MaxEpoch

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

VARIABLES epoch, quota, served, curtailed, unplaced

vars == <<epoch, quota, served, curtailed, unplaced>>

Typing ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ quota \in [Feeders -> 0..Load]
    /\ served \in [Feeders -> 0..Load]
    /\ curtailed \in [Feeders -> 0..Load]
    /\ unplaced \in [Feeders -> 0..Load]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ quota = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ served = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ curtailed = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ unplaced = [f \in Feeders |-> Load]

\* The control room publishes a new shedding plan under a strictly newer epoch
\* number.  The plan only changes how much each feeder is allowed to draw; it
\* never invents or destroys demand.
Republish(e, q) ==
    /\ e > epoch
    /\ epoch' = e
    /\ quota' = [f \in Feeders |-> q]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, curtailed, unplaced>>

\* A block of demand is energised, but only within the feeder's standing quota.
Energise(f) ==
    /\ unplaced[f] > 0
    /\ served[f] < quota[f]
    /\ served' = [served EXCEPT ![f] = served[f] + 1]
    /\ unplaced' = [unplaced EXCEPT ![f] = unplaced[f] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quota, curtailed>>

\* Demand beyond the quota is curtailed rather than dropped from the books.
Curtail(f) ==
    /\ unplaced[f] > 0
    /\ served[f] >= quota[f]
    /\ curtailed' = [curtailed EXCEPT ![f] = curtailed[f] + 1]
    /\ unplaced' = [unplaced EXCEPT ![f] = unplaced[f] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quota, served>>

\* When a newer plan raises a feeder's quota, curtailed blocks are picked back
\* up one at a time.  Feeders are slow, so this can lag the plan by a long way.
Restore(f) ==
    /\ curtailed[f] > 0
    /\ served[f] < quota[f]
    /\ curtailed' = [curtailed EXCEPT ![f] = curtailed[f] - 1]
    /\ served' = [served EXCEPT ![f] = served[f] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quota, unplaced>>

Steady ==
    /\ \A f \in Feeders : unplaced[f] = 0 /\ served[f] >= quota[f]
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in 1..MaxEpoch, q \in 0..Load : Republish(e, q)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Energise(f) \/ Curtail(f) \/ Restore(f)
    \/ Steady

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every block of demand on the books is in exactly one of the three states,
\* through any number of republished plans: the grid neither invents load nor
\* loses track of load it has already curtailed.
DemandConserved ==
    Tally(served, Feeders) + Tally(curtailed, Feeders) + Tally(unplaced, Feeders)
        = Cardinality(Feeders) * Load

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Feeders = {fdrMill, fdrHarbour}
    Load = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2

INVARIANT DemandConserved
nl:
A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder over its distribution feeders. Each feeder arrives at the start of the event with a fixed number of demand blocks on its books, and every one of those blocks must always be accounted for in exactly one of three states: energised, curtailed, or not yet placed.

The control room works by republishing a shedding plan. Each republication carries a strictly newer epoch number and sets the quota each feeder is allowed to draw. A plan only changes quotas; it never invents demand and never writes demand off the books.

A feeder energises an unplaced block whenever doing so keeps it inside its standing quota. A block that would take the feeder past its quota is curtailed instead -- curtailment moves the block out of the unplaced pile and into the curtailed pile, so the block is still carried, not discarded. When a newer plan raises a feeder's quota, the feeder picks curtailed blocks back up one at a time and energises them. Feeders here are slow but never fail: a feeder can lag a long way behind the plan the control room has published, and blocks can sit unplaced or curtailed for an arbitrarily long time, but no feeder ever stops responding altogether. Once every feeder has placed all its blocks and is drawing at least its quota, the grid is steady.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The energised, curtailed and unplaced blocks across all feeders always add up to exactly the demand the event started with, through any number of republished plans.

---- MODULE W4Od0m2p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cases, Slots, Registries, NoSlot

ASSUME NoSlot \notin Slots

VARIABLES stage, ballot, wanted, booked, retried

vars == <<stage, ballot, wanted, booked, retried>>

Typing ==
    /\ stage \in [Cases -> {"unlisted", "polling", "listed", "dropped"}]
    /\ ballot \in [Cases -> [Registries -> {"silent", "yes", "no"}]]
    /\ wanted \in [Cases -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ booked \in [Slots -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ retried \subseteq Cases

Init ==
    /\ stage = [c \in Cases |-> "unlisted"]
    /\ ballot = [c \in Cases |-> [r \in Registries |-> "silent"]]
    /\ wanted = [c \in Cases |-> NoSlot]
    /\ booked = [k \in Slots |-> FALSE]
    /\ retried = {}

\* The scheduler opens a poll for a case against a theatre slot that is not
\* already booked and that no other case is currently polling for.
OpenPoll(c, k) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "unlisted"
    /\ ~booked[k]
    /\ \A d \in Cases : ~(stage[d] = "polling" /\ wanted[d] = k)
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "polling"]
    /\ wanted' = [wanted EXCEPT ![c] = k]
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = [r \in Registries |-> "silent"]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, retried>>

\* Each registry -- anaesthetics, nursing, theatre stores -- answers for its
\* own resources.  Registries here are slow but never fail, so an answer can
\* take arbitrarily long to arrive but always arrives in the end.
Answer(r, c, v) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "polling"
    /\ ballot[c][r] = "silent"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c][r] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, wanted, booked, retried>>

\* The case is listed only once every registry has answered yes.
Commit(c) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "polling"
    /\ \A r \in Registries : ballot[c][r] = "yes"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "listed"]
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![wanted[c]] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, wanted, retried>>

\* One refusal is enough to take the whole listing down and free the slot.
Abort(c) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "polling"
    /\ \E r \in Registries : ballot[c][r] = "no"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "dropped"]
    /\ wanted' = [wanted EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, booked, retried>>

\* A dropped case gets one further attempt, and one only, so the diary cannot
\* churn for ever.
Relist(c) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "dropped"
    /\ c \notin retried
    /\ retried' = retried \cup {c}
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "unlisted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, wanted, booked>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A c \in Cases : stage[c] \in {"listed", "dropped"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cases, k \in Slots : OpenPoll(c, k)
    \/ \E r \in Registries, c \in Cases, v \in {"yes", "no"} : Answer(r, c, v)
    \/ \E c \in Cases : Commit(c) \/ Abort(c) \/ Relist(c)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Registries, c \in Cases, v \in {"yes", "no"} : Answer(r, c, v))
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Cases : Commit(c))
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Cases : Abort(c))

\* Two cases are never listed into the same theatre slot.
NoDoubleListing ==
    \A c, d \in Cases :
        (stage[c] = "listed" /\ stage[d] = "listed" /\ wanted[c] = wanted[d]) => c = d

EveryPollEventuallySettles ==
    \A c \in Cases :
        (stage[c] = "polling") ~> (stage[c] = "listed" \/ stage[c] = "dropped")

====
nl:
A hospital lists its operating theatre work by agreeing each case across several registries at once. A case can only be listed into a theatre slot if the anaesthetics registry and the nursing registry both agree they can staff it, so the scheduler runs the listing as a two-phase agreement rather than writing the booking straight into the diary.

The scheduler opens a poll for an unlisted case against a theatre slot that is not already booked and that no other case is currently polling for. Opening the poll clears every registry's answer for that case. Each registry then answers for its own resources, yes or no. Registries here are slow but never fail: an answer can take arbitrarily long to come back, but it always comes back in the end.

The case is listed only once every registry has answered yes, and listing marks the slot as booked. A single refusal is enough to take the whole listing down: the case is dropped and gives up its claim on the slot, so the slot is available to be polled for again. A dropped case can be put back on the unlisted pile and tried once more, and once only, so the diary cannot churn for ever. Once every case has either been listed or dropped the diary is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Two cases are never listed into the same theatre slot.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every case that has gone to poll eventually settles, either listed or dropped.

---- MODULE W4Od17m5p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Amendments, Routers, ShedBudget, NoRouter

ASSUME NoRouter \notin Routers

VARIABLES entry, kept, strain, sheds

vars == <<entry, kept, strain, sheds>>

Typing ==
    /\ entry \in [Amendments -> [state : {"draft", "offered", "confirmed"},
                                 by : Routers \cup {NoRouter}]]
    /\ kept \in [Nodes -> SUBSET Amendments]
    /\ strain \subseteq Nodes
    /\ sheds \in [Nodes -> 0..ShedBudget]

Init ==
    /\ entry = [a \in Amendments |-> [state |-> "draft", by |-> NoRouter]]
    /\ kept = [n \in Nodes |-> {}]
    /\ strain = {}
    /\ sheds = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]

\* Two routers run side by side over one pool of manifest nodes; either may
\* raise an amendment, and the amendment carries the router that raised it.
Raise(i, a) ==
    /\ entry[a].state = "draft"
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![a] = [state |-> "offered", by |-> i]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<kept, strain, sheds>>

Spread(n, a) ==
    /\ entry[a].state # "draft"
    /\ a \notin kept[n]
    /\ kept' = [kept EXCEPT ![n] = kept[n] \cup {a}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, strain, sheds>>

\* The pool confirms an amendment back to the router that raised it only once
\* a strict majority of the manifest nodes are holding it.
Confirm(a) ==
    /\ entry[a].state = "offered"
    /\ 2 * Cardinality({n \in Nodes : a \in kept[n]}) > Cardinality(Nodes)
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![a].state = "confirmed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<kept, strain, sheds>>

Squeeze(n) ==
    /\ n \notin strain
    /\ strain' = strain \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, kept, sheds>>

\* A node under memory pressure makes room for the other router's traffic, but
\* it will only drop an amendment the pool has not yet confirmed.
Shed(n, a) ==
    /\ n \in strain
    /\ sheds[n] < ShedBudget
    /\ a \in kept[n]
    /\ entry[a].state # "confirmed"
    /\ kept' = [kept EXCEPT ![n] = kept[n] \ {a}]
    /\ sheds' = [sheds EXCEPT ![n] = sheds[n] + 1]
    /\ strain' = strain \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED entry

Idle ==
    /\ \A a \in Amendments : entry[a].state = "confirmed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Routers, a \in Amendments : Raise(i, a)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, a \in Amendments : Spread(n, a) \/ Shed(n, a)
    \/ \E a \in Amendments : Confirm(a)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Squeeze(n)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* An amendment the pool has confirmed to a router is still held by a majority
\* of the manifest nodes, so a confirmed change is never squeezed back out.
NoLostAmendment ==
    \A a \in Amendments :
        (entry[a].state = "confirmed") =>
            (2 * Cardinality({n \in Nodes : a \in kept[n]}) > Cardinality(Nodes))

====
nl:
An airport baggage router keeps its bag manifest on a pool of manifest nodes rather than in one place. Two independent router instances run side by side over that same pool -- one driving the north pier, one the south -- and either of them may raise an amendment to the shared manifest, such as a reroute or a priority change. Raising an amendment records which router raised it and puts the amendment on offer.

An amendment on offer spreads across the pool one node at a time. The pool confirms it back to the router that raised it only once a strict majority of the manifest nodes are holding it. Confirmation is what a router treats as the amendment having taken effect: it will report the bag as rerouted on that basis and will never raise the amendment again, so a confirmed amendment that later vanished from the pool would be an update silently lost.

Manifest nodes are small and the two routers' traffic competes for the same memory. A node can come under pressure, and a node under pressure makes room by dropping one amendment it is holding; each node has a small budget of such drops. A node will only drop an amendment the pool has not yet confirmed. Once every amendment has been confirmed the pool is idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every amendment the pool has confirmed to a router is still held by a majority of the manifest nodes, so a confirmed change to the shared manifest is never squeezed back out under the other router's traffic.

---- MODULE W4Od8m5p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Places, Registrars, NoStudent, NoPlace

ASSUME NoStudent \notin Students /\ NoPlace \notin Places

VARIABLES record, pencil, offline, slip

vars == <<record, pencil, offline, slip>>

Typing ==
    /\ record \in [Students -> [state : {"browsing", "waiting", "enrolled"},
                                place : Places \cup {NoPlace}]]
    /\ pencil \in [Registrars -> [Places -> Students \cup {NoStudent}]]
    /\ offline \subseteq Registrars
    /\ slip \in [Students -> {"none", "issued", "spent"}]

Marks(s, k) == {r \in Registrars : pencil[r][k] = s}

Init ==
    /\ record = [s \in Students |-> [state |-> "browsing", place |-> NoPlace]]
    /\ pencil = [r \in Registrars |-> [k \in Places |-> NoStudent]]
    /\ offline = {}
    /\ slip = [s \in Students |-> "none"]

\* Registration issues each student one enrolment slip.
IssueSlip(s) ==
    /\ slip[s] = "none"
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![s] = "issued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, pencil, offline>>

\* A student spends the slip applying for a place nobody else is claiming.
Apply(s, k) ==
    /\ record[s].state = "browsing"
    /\ slip[s] = "issued"
    /\ \A t \in Students : record[t].place # k
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![s] = [state |-> "waiting", place |-> k]]
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![s] = "spent"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pencil, offline>>

\* Each registrar keeps its own roll and pencils an applicant into a place
\* only while its own line for that place is still blank.  No registrar can
\* see any other registrar's roll.
Mark(r, s) ==
    /\ r \notin offline
    /\ record[s].state = "waiting"
    /\ pencil[r][record[s].place] = NoStudent
    /\ pencil' = [pencil EXCEPT ![r][record[s].place] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, offline, slip>>

\* Enrolment needs a strict majority of the registrars to have pencilled the
\* same student into the same place, so two rolls can never both carry a
\* majority for different students in one place.
Enrol(s) ==
    /\ record[s].state = "waiting"
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Marks(s, record[s].place)) > Cardinality(Registrars)
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![s].state = "enrolled"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pencil, offline, slip>>

\* One registrar's node may drop off the network without saying so.
DropOff(r) ==
    /\ offline = {}
    /\ offline' = {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, pencil, slip>>

Closed ==
    /\ \A s \in Students : record[s].state = "enrolled"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students, k \in Places : Apply(s, k)
    \/ \E s \in Students : IssueSlip(s)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars, s \in Students : Mark(r, s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Enrol(s)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : DropOff(r)
    \/ Closed

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Registrars, s \in Students : Mark(r, s))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Students : Enrol(s))

\* Every enrolled student holds a majority of the registrars' rolls for the
\* place they hold, so no place is ever enrolled to two students.
NoDoubleEnrolment ==
    \A s \in Students :
        (record[s].state = "enrolled") =>
            (2 * Cardinality(Marks(s, record[s].place)) > Cardinality(Registrars))

EveryApplicantEventuallyEnrolled ==
    \A s \in Students : (record[s].state = "waiting") ~> (record[s].state = "enrolled")

====
nl:
A university runs course registration across several registrar nodes, each of which keeps its own roll. No registrar can see any other registrar's roll, and no single registrar can enrol anybody on its own.

Registration issues each student a single enrolment slip. A student who is browsing spends that slip applying for a place that no other student is currently claiming, and then waits. Each registrar pencils the applicant into the place on its own roll, but only while its own line for that place is still blank -- once a registrar has pencilled somebody into a place, that line stays as it is.

Enrolment needs a strict majority of the registrars to have pencilled the same student into the same place. Because any two majorities of the registrars share at least one member, and no registrar ever writes two names on one line, two students can never both collect a majority for the same place.

Registrar nodes on a campus network are not reliable. A single registrar may drop off the network without saying so and pencils nothing further, while the rest carry on; a majority of three is two, so registration still completes with one registrar gone. Once every student is enrolled, registration is closed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every enrolled student holds a majority of the registrars' rolls for the place they have been given, so the same place is never enrolled to two students.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every student who applies and waits is eventually enrolled.

---- MODULE W4Od14m1p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, ChurnBudget, NoDrone

ASSUME NoDrone \notin Drones

VARIABLES stance, baton, ring, churn

vars == <<stance, baton, ring, churn>>

Typing ==
    /\ stance \in [Drones -> {"aloft", "waiting", "burst"}]
    /\ baton \in Drones \cup {NoDrone}
    /\ ring \subseteq Drones
    /\ churn \in 0..ChurnBudget

Init ==
    /\ stance = [d \in Drones |-> "aloft"]
    /\ baton = NoDrone
    /\ ring = {}
    /\ churn = 0

\* The ring is not a fixed shape: drones join and drop out of the relay
\* rotation as the fire front moves, so its size changes while it is running.
\* The first drone to join is handed the baton.
Join(d) ==
    /\ d \notin ring
    /\ churn < ChurnBudget
    /\ ring' = ring \cup {d}
    /\ churn' = churn + 1
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![d] = "waiting"]
    /\ baton' = IF ring = {} THEN d ELSE baton

\* A drone may only leave while it is not mid-burst and is not the one holding
\* the baton, so the baton is never carried out of the rotation.
Drop(d) ==
    /\ d \in ring
    /\ stance[d] # "burst"
    /\ baton # d
    /\ ring' = ring \ {d}
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![d] = "aloft"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, churn>>

\* The baton is handed on to any other drone still in the rotation, but never
\* while its holder has the relay open.
Pass(e) ==
    /\ baton \in ring
    /\ stance[baton] # "burst"
    /\ e \in ring
    /\ e # baton
    /\ baton' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stance, ring, churn>>

\* Only the drone holding the baton may open the relay.
OpenRelay(d) ==
    /\ baton = d
    /\ d \in ring
    /\ stance[d] = "waiting"
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![d] = "burst"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, ring, churn>>

CloseRelay(d) ==
    /\ stance[d] = "burst"
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![d] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, ring, churn>>

Hover ==
    /\ churn = ChurnBudget
    /\ ring = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Join(d) \/ Drop(d) \/ OpenRelay(d) \/ CloseRelay(d)
    \/ \E e \in Drones : Pass(e)
    \/ Hover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* However the rotation grows and shrinks under it, two drones never have the
\* relay open at the same time.
RelayExclusion ==
    \A c, d \in Drones :
        (stance[c] = "burst" /\ stance[d] = "burst") => c = d

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {drnAlpha, drnBravo, drnCharlie}
    ChurnBudget = 6
    NoDrone = nilDrone

INVARIANT RelayExclusion
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm relays its imagery to the incident command aircraft over one narrowband channel. Only one drone at a time may have that relay open; two drones bursting at once drown each other out and command loses both feeds. The swarm arranges the turn-taking by passing a baton around a rotation.

The rotation is not a fixed shape. Drones join and drop out of it while it is running as the fire front moves and aircraft are re-tasked, so its size changes underneath the baton; the swarm allows only a limited amount of this churn during a single sortie. The first drone to join is handed the baton. A drone may only drop out while it is not mid-burst and is not the drone currently holding the baton, so the baton is never carried out of the rotation by a departing aircraft.

The baton is handed on to any other drone still in the rotation, but never while its holder has the relay open. Only the drone holding the baton may open the relay, and only if it is in the rotation and waiting for its turn; when it is done it closes the relay and goes back to waiting. Once the sortie's churn allowance is spent and the rotation is empty, the swarm just hovers.

SAFETY PROPERTY: However the rotation grows and shrinks underneath it, two drones never have the relay open at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od16m5p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Amendments, Pharmacists, ForceBudget, NoPharm

ASSUME NoPharm \notin Pharmacists

Weight(sign, duty) == Cardinality(sign) + (IF duty \in sign THEN 1 ELSE 0)

VARIABLES chart, signed, duty, forces

vars == <<chart, signed, duty, forces>>

Typing ==
    /\ chart \in [Amendments -> [state : {"drafted", "circulating", "entered"},
                                under : Pharmacists \cup {NoPharm}]]
    /\ signed \in [Amendments -> SUBSET Pharmacists]
    /\ duty \in Pharmacists
    /\ forces \in 0..ForceBudget

\* The duty pharmacist's signature is the privileged one: it is counted twice
\* when weighing an amendment, so the bar is a weighted majority.
Bar == Cardinality(Pharmacists) + 1

Init ==
    /\ chart = [a \in Amendments |-> [state |-> "drafted", under |-> NoPharm]]
    /\ signed = [a \in Amendments |-> {}]
    /\ duty = CHOOSE p \in Pharmacists : TRUE
    /\ forces = 0

Circulate(a) ==
    /\ chart[a].state = "drafted"
    /\ chart' = [chart EXCEPT ![a].state = "circulating"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<signed, duty, forces>>

Sign(p, a) ==
    /\ chart[a].state = "circulating"
    /\ p \notin signed[a]
    /\ signed' = [signed EXCEPT ![a] = signed[a] \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, duty, forces>>

\* An amendment goes onto the patient chart only once the signatures on it
\* clear the weighted bar.
Enter(a) ==
    /\ chart[a].state = "circulating"
    /\ 2 * Weight(signed[a], duty) > Bar
    /\ chart' = [chart EXCEPT ![a] = [state |-> "entered", under |-> duty]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<signed, duty, forces>>

\* The privileged override: the duty pharmacist may countersign an amendment
\* directly rather than waiting for it to come round the rota.  It still has
\* to clear the same weighted bar afterwards, and the override may only be
\* used a fixed number of times in a shift.
Override(a) ==
    /\ chart[a].state = "circulating"
    /\ duty \notin signed[a]
    /\ forces < ForceBudget
    /\ signed' = [signed EXCEPT ![a] = signed[a] \cup {duty}]
    /\ forces' = forces + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, duty>>

\* The duty pharmacist changes at handover.  Signatures already collected stay
\* where they are; only the weighting moves.
Handover(p) ==
    /\ p # duty
    /\ \A a \in Amendments : chart[a].state # "circulating"
    /\ duty' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, signed, forces>>

Shut ==
    /\ \A a \in Amendments : chart[a].state = "entered"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Amendments : Circulate(a) \/ Enter(a) \/ Override(a)
    \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, a \in Amendments : Sign(p, a)
    \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : Handover(p)
    \/ Shut

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every amendment that has reached the patient chart still carries signatures
\* clearing the weighted bar, so a later amendment can never quietly displace
\* the authority an entered one was written on.
NoLostAmendment ==
    \A a \in Amendments :
        (chart[a].state = "entered") => (2 * Weight(signed[a], chart[a].under) > Bar)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Amendments = {amdDose, amdSubstitute}
    Pharmacists = {phMara, phOkoye, phRuiz}
    ForceBudget = 1
    NoPharm = nilPharm

INVARIANT NoLostAmendment
nl:
A hospital pharmacy enters amendments to a patient's dispensing chart -- a dose change, a substitution -- only on the agreement of several pharmacists rather than on one person's say-so. An amendment is drafted, then put into circulation, and pharmacists sign it as it comes round the rota.

The signatures are weighed rather than simply counted. The pharmacist on duty holds a privileged signature: theirs is counted twice. An amendment goes onto the chart only once the signatures on it clear a weighted bar of more than half of the count of all pharmacists plus one, and the chart records which pharmacist was on duty when the amendment was entered, because that is the weighting the entry was authorised under.

The duty pharmacist may also override the rota: rather than waiting for an amendment to come round, they may countersign it directly. The override does not lower the bar -- the amendment still has to clear the same weighted bar afterwards -- and the override may only be used a fixed number of times in a shift. Duty changes hands at handover, which is only done while nothing is in circulation; signatures already collected stay exactly where they are and only the weighting for future entries moves. Once every amendment has been entered the chart is shut.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every amendment that has reached the patient chart still carries signatures clearing the weighted bar it was entered under, so no later amendment or handover can quietly displace the authority an entered amendment was written on.

---- MODULE W4Od1m4p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, Windows, Controllers, BoardCap, NoWindow, NoFlight

ASSUME NoWindow \notin Windows /\ NoFlight \notin Flights

VARIABLES flight, strip, tower, board

vars == <<flight, strip, tower, board>>

Typing ==
    /\ flight \in [Flights -> [state : {"held", "queued", "cleared", "bumped"},
                               slot : Windows \cup {NoWindow}]]
    /\ strip \in [Windows -> [state : {"open", "issued"},
                              to : Flights \cup {NoFlight}]]
    /\ tower \in [Controllers -> {"staffed", "silent"}]
    /\ board \subseteq Flights

Init ==
    /\ flight = [f \in Flights |-> [state |-> "held", slot |-> NoWindow]]
    /\ strip = [w \in Windows |-> [state |-> "open", to |-> NoFlight]]
    /\ tower = [c \in Controllers |-> "staffed"]
    /\ board = {}

\* A held flight asks for a departure window and goes onto the paper strip
\* board.  The board holds only so many strips: while it is full nothing
\* further can be requested, which is the backpressure on the holding stacks.
Request(f, w) ==
    /\ flight[f].state = "held"
    /\ strip[w].state = "open"
    /\ Cardinality(board) < BoardCap
    /\ flight' = [flight EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "queued", slot |-> w]]
    /\ board' = board \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<strip, tower>>

\* Issuing the clearance is the irreversible step: it goes out over the air
\* and to the departure sequencer, so a window that has been issued can never
\* be issued again, to this flight or to any other.
Issue(f, c) ==
    /\ tower[c] = "staffed"
    /\ flight[f].state = "queued"
    /\ strip[flight[f].slot].state = "open"
    /\ strip' = [strip EXCEPT ![flight[f].slot] = [state |-> "issued", to |-> f]]
    /\ flight' = [flight EXCEPT ![f].state = "cleared"]
    /\ board' = board \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED tower

\* Two flights may have asked for the same window; whichever loses the race is
\* bumped off the board and can ask again for a different window.
Bump(f) ==
    /\ flight[f].state = "queued"
    /\ strip[flight[f].slot].state = "issued"
    /\ strip[flight[f].slot].to # f
    /\ flight' = [flight EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "bumped", slot |-> NoWindow]]
    /\ board' = board \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<strip, tower>>

\* One controller position may go quiet without anybody noticing.
FallSilent(c) ==
    /\ \A d \in Controllers : tower[d] = "staffed"
    /\ Cardinality(Controllers) > 1
    /\ tower' = [tower EXCEPT ![c] = "silent"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<flight, strip, board>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A f \in Flights : flight[f].state \in {"cleared", "bumped"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights, w \in Windows : Request(f, w)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, c \in Controllers : Issue(f, c)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Bump(f)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : FallSilent(c)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E f \in Flights, c \in Controllers : Issue(f, c))
    /\ WF_vars(\E f \in Flights : Bump(f))

\* A departure window that has been issued was issued to exactly one flight,
\* and that flight is the one holding the clearance.
ClearanceIssuedOnce ==
    \A w \in Windows :
        (strip[w].state = "issued") =>
            (Cardinality({f \in Flights : flight[f].state = "cleared"
                                          /\ flight[f].slot = w}) = 1)

EveryStripEventuallyResolves ==
    \A f \in Flights :
        (flight[f].state = "queued") ~>
            (flight[f].state = "cleared" \/ flight[f].state = "bumped")

====
nl:
An airport allocates departure windows from the tower. A flight held on the ground asks for a window and goes onto the paper strip board. The board holds only so many strips at once: while it is full nothing further can be requested and the holding stacks simply wait, which is the backpressure that stops the tower taking on more sequencing than it can work.

Issuing a clearance against a window is the irreversible step. The clearance goes out over the air and into the departure sequencer downstream, so once a window has been issued it can never be issued again -- not to another flight, and not a second time to the same flight. A controller issues a clearance for a queued flight only while that flight's window is still open, and the strip then records which flight the window went to.

Nothing stops two flights asking for the same window, because the request only checks that the window is open at the time of asking. Whichever flight loses that race finds its window already issued to somebody else; it is bumped off the board and can ask again for a different window.

Tower positions are not always covered. One controller position may go quiet without anybody noticing and issues nothing further, while the remaining position carries on working the board. Once every flight has either been cleared or bumped the board is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A departure window that has been issued was issued to exactly one flight, and that flight is the one holding the clearance for it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every flight whose strip is on the board is eventually resolved, either cleared into its window or bumped off it.

---- MODULE W4Od14m3p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Ships, Missions, MaxEpoch, OrderCap

Epochs == 1..MaxEpoch
Orders == [tgt : Ships, mis : Missions, ep : Epochs]

VARIABLES ship, wire, fired, lead

vars == <<ship, wire, fired, lead>>

Typing ==
    /\ ship \in [Ships -> [state : {"flying", "scuttled"}, fence : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ wire \subseteq Orders
    /\ fired \subseteq [tgt : Ships, mis : Missions]
    /\ lead \in [Missions -> 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ ship = [s \in Ships |-> [state |-> "flying", fence |-> 0]]
    /\ wire = {}
    /\ fired = {}
    /\ lead = [m \in Missions |-> 0]

\* Two mission desks fly out of the same pool of airframes.  Each desk elects
\* its own lead station, and an election takes an epoch newer than any epoch
\* either desk has yet elected under, so the two desks share one epoch line.
Elect(m, e) ==
    /\ \A k \in Missions : e > lead[k]
    /\ lead' = [lead EXCEPT ![m] = e]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, wire, fired>>

\* A lead station puts a scuttle order on the wire, stamped with its epoch.
\* Either desk may order any ship in the shared pool.
Order(m, s) ==
    /\ lead[m] > 0
    /\ Cardinality(wire) < OrderCap
    /\ wire' = wire \cup {[tgt |-> s, mis |-> m, ep |-> lead[m]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, fired, lead>>

\* Cutting the flight termination charge is irreversible: the airframe is gone
\* and no second order can be carried out against it.  The ship also fences
\* itself at the epoch it acted on, so a later order under an older epoch --
\* which is what a superseded lead station would send -- is refused.
Cut(o) ==
    /\ o \in wire
    /\ ship[o.tgt].state = "flying"
    /\ o.ep >= ship[o.tgt].fence
    /\ ship' = [ship EXCEPT ![o.tgt] = [state |-> "scuttled", fence |-> o.ep]]
    /\ fired' = fired \cup {[tgt |-> o.tgt, mis |-> o.mis]}
    /\ wire' = wire \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED lead

Refuse(o) ==
    /\ o \in wire
    /\ \/ ship[o.tgt].state = "scuttled"
       \/ o.ep < ship[o.tgt].fence
    /\ wire' = wire \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, fired, lead>>

Silent ==
    /\ wire = {}
    /\ \A m \in Missions : lead[m] = MaxEpoch \/ lead[m] = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Missions, e \in Epochs : Elect(m, e)
    \/ \E m \in Missions, s \in Ships : Order(m, s)
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Cut(o) \/ Refuse(o)
    \/ Silent

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A scuttled airframe was cut exactly once, whichever desk's lead station got
\* its order carried out first.
CutAtMostOnce ==
    \A s \in Ships :
        (ship[s].state = "scuttled") =>
            (Cardinality({x \in fired : x.tgt = s}) = 1)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Ships = {shpKite, shpTern}
    Missions = {msnRidge, msnValley}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    OrderCap = 2

INVARIANT CutAtMostOnce
nl:
Two wildfire mission desks fly out of the same pool of surveillance airframes. The desks are run independently -- one covers the ridge, one the valley -- but they draw their aircraft from one shared pool, so either desk may find itself commanding any airframe in it.

Each desk elects its own lead station, and an election takes an epoch number strictly newer than any epoch either desk has yet elected under, so the two desks share a single epoch line even though they run separately. A lead station may put a flight-termination order onto the shared wire, stamped with the epoch that station holds. The wire holds only a limited number of outstanding orders.

Cutting an airframe's flight-termination charge is irreversible: the aircraft is gone, and no second order can ever be carried out against it. When an airframe acts on an order, it also fences itself at the epoch it acted on, so a later order stamped with an older epoch -- which is exactly what a lead station that has been superseded by the other desk would send -- is refused rather than carried out. An order aimed at an airframe that has already been cut, or stamped below that airframe's fence, is taken off the wire and refused.

SAFETY PROPERTY: An airframe that has been scuttled was cut exactly once, whichever desk's lead station got its order carried out first.

---- MODULE W4Od16m3p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Scripts, Bays, Stations, MaxEpoch, ChurnCap, NoBay, NoScript, NoStation

ASSUME NoBay \notin Bays /\ NoScript \notin Scripts /\ NoStation \notin Stations

Epochs == 1..MaxEpoch

VARIABLES script, bay, chief, claim, churn

vars == <<script, bay, chief, claim, churn>>

Typing ==
    /\ script \in [Scripts -> [state : {"received", "assigned", "dispensed"},
                               bay : Bays \cup {NoBay}]]
    /\ bay \in [Bays -> [state : {"offline", "free", "busy"},
                         holder : Scripts \cup {NoScript}]]
    /\ chief \in [ctl : Stations \cup {NoStation}, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ claim \in [Stations -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ churn \in 0..ChurnCap

InService == {k \in Bays : bay[k].state # "offline"}

Init ==
    /\ script = [s \in Scripts |-> [state |-> "received", bay |-> NoBay]]
    /\ bay = [k \in Bays |-> [state |-> "free", holder |-> NoScript]]
    /\ chief = [ctl |-> NoStation, ep |-> 0]
    /\ claim = [c \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ churn = 0

\* The dispensing floor is driven by whichever control station currently holds
\* the floor.  A station claims an epoch newer than any yet claimed; taking the
\* floor is a separate step, so a failover leaves the floor briefly unheld.
Claim(c, e) ==
    /\ \A d \in Stations : e > claim[d]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = e]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<script, bay, chief, churn>>

TakeFloor(c) ==
    /\ claim[c] > chief.ep
    /\ chief' = [ctl |-> c, ep |-> claim[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<script, bay, claim, churn>>

\* Robot bays are taken out of service for cartridge changes and brought back,
\* so the floor's capacity changes while it is running.  A bay is only taken
\* out while it is free, and the floor never drops below one bay in service.
CloseBay(k) ==
    /\ bay[k].state = "free"
    /\ Cardinality(InService) > 1
    /\ churn < ChurnCap
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![k].state = "offline"]
    /\ churn' = churn + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<script, chief, claim>>

OpenBay(k) ==
    /\ bay[k].state = "offline"
    /\ churn < ChurnCap
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![k].state = "free"]
    /\ churn' = churn + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<script, chief, claim>>

\* Only the station holding the floor allocates work, and only into a bay that
\* is in service and standing free.  The bay and the script are written in the
\* same movement, so the two sides of the allocation cannot come apart.
Allocate(s, k) ==
    /\ chief.ctl # NoStation
    /\ script[s].state = "received"
    /\ bay[k].state = "free"
    /\ script' = [script EXCEPT ![s] = [state |-> "assigned", bay |-> k]]
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![k] = [state |-> "busy", holder |-> s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chief, claim, churn>>

Dispense(s) ==
    /\ script[s].state = "assigned"
    /\ script' = [script EXCEPT ![s].state = "dispensed"]
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![script[s].bay] = [state |-> "free", holder |-> NoScript]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chief, claim, churn>>

Closed ==
    /\ \A s \in Scripts : script[s].state = "dispensed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Stations, e \in Epochs : Claim(c, e)
    \/ \E c \in Stations : TakeFloor(c)
    \/ \E k \in Bays : CloseBay(k) \/ OpenBay(k)
    \/ \E s \in Scripts, k \in Bays : Allocate(s, k)
    \/ \E s \in Scripts : Dispense(s)
    \/ Closed

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Stations, e \in Epochs : Claim(c, e))
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Stations : TakeFloor(c))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Scripts, k \in Bays : Allocate(s, k))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Scripts : Dispense(s))

\* A script that has been allocated is held by exactly one robot bay, so no bay
\* is ever carrying two prescriptions at once however the floor is re-sized.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A s \in Scripts :
        (script[s].state = "assigned") =>
            (Cardinality({k \in Bays : bay[k].holder = s}) = 1)

EveryScriptEventuallyDispensed ==
    \A s \in Scripts : (script[s].state = "received") ~> (script[s].state = "dispensed")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Scripts = {scrAmox, scrWarf}
    Bays = {bayOne, bayTwo}
    Stations = {stnFront, stnBack}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    ChurnCap = 2
    NoBay = nilBay
    NoScript = nilScript
    NoStation = nilStation

INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY EveryScriptEventuallyDispensed
nl:
A hospital pharmacy dispenses from a floor of robot bays. Prescriptions arrive on the queue and have to be allocated to a bay before the robot can pick and label them.

The floor is driven by whichever control station currently holds it. A station takes the floor by claiming an epoch number strictly newer than any epoch yet claimed by any station, and then taking the floor under that claim. Claiming and taking are separate steps, so a failover leaves the floor briefly unheld, and only a station that actually holds the floor allocates work.

The floor's capacity changes while it is running. Robot bays are taken out of service for cartridge changes and brought back afterwards; a bay is only taken out while it is standing free, the floor never drops below one bay in service, and the number of such changes in a session is limited.

Allocation writes both sides at once: the script records the bay it has been given and the bay records the script it is carrying, so the two halves of the allocation cannot come apart. A bay must be in service and standing free to be allocated. When the robot finishes, the script is dispensed and the bay goes back to free. Once every script has been dispensed the floor is closed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A script that has been allocated is held by exactly one robot bay, so no bay is ever carrying two prescriptions at once however the floor is re-sized underneath it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every prescription that arrives on the queue is eventually dispensed.

---- MODULE W4Od7m4p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Moves, Stacks, QueueCap, MaxRev, ForceCap

VARIABLES move, ledger, yardRev, forced

vars == <<move, ledger, yardRev, forced>>

Typing ==
    /\ move \in [Moves -> [state : {"waiting", "queued", "posted", "bounced"},
                           base : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ ledger \in [Stacks -> SUBSET Moves]
    /\ yardRev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ forced \in 0..ForceCap

Queued == {m \in Moves : move[m].state = "queued"}

Init ==
    /\ move = [m \in Moves |-> [state |-> "waiting", base |-> 0]]
    /\ ledger = [t \in Stacks |-> {}]
    /\ yardRev = 0
    /\ forced = 0

\* The crane order queue is short: while it is full the planners cannot lodge
\* another move and simply have to wait, which is the backpressure that stops
\* the plan running ahead of the cranes.  Lodging stamps the yard revision the
\* planner read.
Lodge(m) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "waiting"
    /\ Cardinality(Queued) < QueueCap
    /\ yardRev < MaxRev
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m] = [state |-> "queued", base |-> yardRev]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, yardRev, forced>>

\* A move is posted against a stack only while the revision its planner read is
\* still the standing yard revision.  Posting adds to the stack's ledger; it
\* never rewrites the ledger wholesale, so nothing already there is displaced.
Post(m, t) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "queued"
    /\ move[m].base = yardRev
    /\ yardRev < MaxRev
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![t] = ledger[t] \cup {m}]
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m].state = "posted"]
    /\ yardRev' = yardRev + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED forced

Bounce(m) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "queued"
    /\ move[m].base # yardRev
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m].state = "bounced"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, yardRev, forced>>

\* The privileged override: the yard superintendent may push a stale move
\* through anyway.  It still only adds to the stack's ledger, and there are
\* only so many overrides in a shift.
Force(m, t) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "queued"
    /\ move[m].base # yardRev
    /\ forced < ForceCap
    /\ yardRev < MaxRev
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![t] = ledger[t] \cup {m}]
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m].state = "posted"]
    /\ yardRev' = yardRev + 1
    /\ forced' = forced + 1

\* Ledgers are trimmed of orders that never went anywhere.
Compact(t) ==
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![t] = {m \in ledger[t] : move[m].state = "posted"}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<move, yardRev, forced>>

Relodge(m) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "bounced"
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m].state = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, yardRev, forced>>

Idle ==
    /\ yardRev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Moves : Lodge(m) \/ Bounce(m) \/ Relodge(m)
    \/ \E m \in Moves, t \in Stacks : Post(m, t) \/ Force(m, t)
    \/ \E t \in Stacks : Compact(t)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every move that has been posted still stands in exactly one stack ledger, so
\* no posted crane order is ever carried away by a later posting or a trim.
NoLostMove ==
    \A m \in Moves :
        (move[m].state = "posted") =>
            (Cardinality({t \in Stacks : m \in ledger[t]}) = 1)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Moves = {mvBox14, mvBox27, mvBox31}
    Stacks = {stkQuay, stkYard}
    QueueCap = 2
    MaxRev = 3
    ForceCap = 1

INVARIANT NoLostMove
nl:
A container-ship crane yard plans its moves against a shared yard ledger, one ledger per stack, recording which crane orders have been booked against that stack.

Planners lodge moves onto a short crane order queue. The queue is deliberately short: while it is full nothing further can be lodged and the planners simply have to wait, which is the backpressure that stops the plan running ahead of what the cranes can work. Lodging a move stamps it with the yard revision the planner read at that moment.

A move is posted against a stack only while the revision its planner read is still the standing yard revision, and posting bumps that revision. Posting adds the move to the stack's ledger rather than rewriting the ledger wholesale, so nothing already booked there is displaced by it. A move whose planner read a revision that has since moved on is bounced rather than posted, and a bounced move can be lodged again.

There is a privileged override: the yard superintendent may push a stale move through anyway when the ship is on the tide. The override still only adds to the stack's ledger, and there are only so many overrides in a shift. Separately, ledgers are trimmed from time to time of orders that never went anywhere.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every move that has been posted still stands in exactly one stack ledger, so no posted crane order is ever carried away by a later posting, an override, or a trim.

---- MODULE W4Od16m6p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Batches, Bins, Horizon, LeaseLen, RevokeCap, NoBatch, NoBin

ASSUME NoBatch \notin Batches /\ NoBin \notin Bins

Clip(n) == IF n < Horizon THEN n ELSE Horizon

VARIABLES batch, lease, clock, revokes

vars == <<batch, lease, clock, revokes>>

Typing ==
    /\ batch \in [Batches -> [state : {"pending", "held", "stored"},
                              bin : Bins \cup {NoBin}]]
    /\ lease \in [Bins -> [holder : Batches \cup {NoBatch}, until : 0..Horizon]]
    /\ clock \in 0..Horizon
    /\ revokes \in 0..RevokeCap

Init ==
    /\ batch = [b \in Batches |-> [state |-> "pending", bin |-> NoBin]]
    /\ lease = [k \in Bins |-> [holder |-> NoBatch, until |-> 0]]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ revokes = 0

\* A pending batch is leased a cold bin that nobody is holding.  The lease runs
\* to a fixed horizon from now, and both sides of it -- the bin's holder and the
\* batch's bin -- are written in the same movement.
Grant(b, k) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "pending"
    /\ lease[k].holder = NoBatch
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b] = [state |-> "held", bin |-> k]]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![k] = [holder |-> b, until |-> Clip(clock + LeaseLen)]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, revokes>>

Store(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "held"
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "stored"]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![batch[b].bin] = [holder |-> NoBatch, until |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, revokes>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, lease, revokes>>

\* A lease that has run out is reclaimed and its batch goes back to pending.
\* Both sides are cleared together, so the bin is never left holding a batch
\* that no longer thinks it has one.
Expire(k) ==
    /\ lease[k].holder # NoBatch
    /\ lease[k].until < clock
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![lease[k].holder] = [state |-> "pending", bin |-> NoBin]]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![k] = [holder |-> NoBatch, until |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, revokes>>

\* The privileged override: the duty pharmacist may pull a lease back early to
\* free a cold bin for an urgent line.  There are only so many in a shift.
Revoke(k) ==
    /\ lease[k].holder # NoBatch
    /\ revokes < RevokeCap
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![lease[k].holder] = [state |-> "pending", bin |-> NoBin]]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![k] = [holder |-> NoBatch, until |-> 0]]
    /\ revokes' = revokes + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Shut ==
    /\ \A b \in Batches : batch[b].state = "stored"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Batches, k \in Bins : Grant(b, k)
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Store(b)
    \/ \E k \in Bins : Expire(k) \/ Revoke(k)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Shut

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Batches, k \in Bins : Grant(b, k))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Batches : Store(b))

\* A batch that is holding a cold bin holds exactly one, so a bin is never
\* leased to two batches at once across an expiry or an early revocation.
NoDoubleLease ==
    \A b \in Batches :
        (batch[b].state = "held") =>
            (Cardinality({k \in Bins : lease[k].holder = b}) = 1)

EveryBatchEventuallyStored ==
    \A b \in Batches : (batch[b].state = "pending") ~> (batch[b].state = "stored")

====
