SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Batches = {btcInsulin, btcVaccine}
    Bins = {binUpper, binLower}
    Horizon = 2
    LeaseLen = 1
    RevokeCap = 1
    NoBatch = nilBatch
    NoBin = nilBin

INVARIANT NoDoubleLease
PROPERTY EveryBatchEventuallyStored
nl:
A hospital pharmacy stores temperature-controlled lines in a small bank of cold bins. A batch waiting to go away has to be given a bin before it can be put down, and a bin can only be carrying one batch at a time.

Bins are handed out on leases with an expiry rather than held indefinitely, because a batch left half-processed would otherwise strand a bin for the rest of the shift. A pending batch is leased a bin that nobody is holding, and the lease runs to a fixed horizon from the moment it is granted. Both sides of the lease -- the bin's record of its holder and the batch's record of its bin -- are written in the same movement, so they cannot come apart.

A lease is reclaimed once the clock has moved strictly past its expiry: the bin is released and the batch goes back to pending to be leased a bin again later. Both sides are cleared together, so a bin is never left holding a batch that no longer thinks it has one. There is also a privileged override: the duty pharmacist may pull a lease back early to free a cold bin for an urgent line, and there are only so many such revocations in a shift. A batch that gets its stock put away before its lease runs out is stored and releases the bin.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A batch that is holding a cold bin holds exactly one, so a bin is never leased to two batches at once across an expiry or an early revocation.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every pending batch is eventually stored away.

---- MODULE W4Od2m7p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Fleets, Total, MaxRev, NoRobot

ASSUME NoRobot \notin Robots

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

VARIABLES pool, rev, drawn, burnt, bid

vars == <<pool, rev, drawn, burnt, bid>>

Typing ==
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ drawn \in [Robots -> 0..Total]
    /\ burnt \in 0..Total
    /\ bid \in [Fleets -> [state : {"idle", "reading"}, base : 0..MaxRev,
                           robot : Robots \cup {NoRobot}]]

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ drawn = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ burnt = 0
    /\ bid = [f \in Fleets |-> [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, robot |-> NoRobot]]

\* Two fleet controllers work the same floor out of one pool of charge
\* allowances.  A controller reads the pool register and the revision stamped
\* on it, then goes away to decide which robot to top up.
Read(f, r) ==
    /\ bid[f].state = "idle"
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rev, robot |-> r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, rev, drawn, burnt>>

\* The write back is a compare-and-swap: it only lands while the revision the
\* controller read is still the one on the register, so the other controller
\* cannot have moved the pool underneath it.  An allowance leaves the pool and
\* arrives on a robot in the same movement.
Commit(f) ==
    /\ bid[f].state = "reading"
    /\ bid[f].base = rev
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ drawn' = [drawn EXCEPT ![bid[f].robot] = drawn[bid[f].robot] + 1]
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, robot |-> NoRobot]]
    /\ UNCHANGED burnt

\* A controller whose read has gone stale abandons the write and starts again.
Retry(f) ==
    /\ bid[f].state = "reading"
    /\ \/ bid[f].base # rev
       \/ pool = 0
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, robot |-> NoRobot]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, rev, drawn, burnt>>

Spend(r) ==
    /\ drawn[r] > 0
    /\ drawn' = [drawn EXCEPT ![r] = drawn[r] - 1]
    /\ burnt' = burnt + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, rev, bid>>

HandBack(r) ==
    /\ drawn[r] > 0
    /\ drawn' = [drawn EXCEPT ![r] = drawn[r] - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, burnt, bid>>

\* Once the register has been stamped for the last time the floor is parked.
Parked ==
    /\ rev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Fleets, r \in Robots : Read(f, r)
    \/ \E f \in Fleets : Commit(f) \/ Retry(f)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Spend(r) \/ HandBack(r)
    \/ Parked

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Charge allowances are never created or destroyed by the two controllers
\* racing each other: what is left in the pool, what the robots are carrying
\* and what has been burnt always add back up to the day's total.
ChargeConserved == pool + Tally(drawn, Robots) + burnt = Total

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {rbtPicker, rbtTug}
    Fleets = {fltDay, fltNight}
    Total = 2
    MaxRev = 3
    NoRobot = nilRobot

INVARIANT ChargeConserved
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet draws its charging allowances for the day from a single shared pool. Two fleet controllers -- the day scheduler and the night scheduler -- run as independent instances but work the same floor and draw from that one pool, so they are constantly racing each other for the same allowances.

The pool is kept in a register carrying a revision stamp. A controller reads the register and the revision on it, then goes away to decide which robot to top up. The write back is a compare-and-swap: it only lands while the revision the controller read is still the one on the register. If the other controller has moved the pool in the meantime, the revision has changed, the write is abandoned, and the controller starts again from a fresh read. A landing write takes one allowance out of the pool and puts it on the chosen robot in the same movement, and bumps the revision.

A robot spends an allowance it is carrying by running a shift on it, which burns the allowance. A robot can also hand an allowance back to the pool unspent when its work is cancelled. Nothing else moves allowances around, and no controller can conjure one. The register carries only so many revision stamps in a day; once the last one has been used the floor is parked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Charge allowances are never created or destroyed by the two controllers racing each other -- what is left in the pool, what the robots are carrying and what has been burnt always add back up to the day's total.

---- MODULE W4Od16m0p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Deliveries, Cap, MaxRev

VARIABLES delivery, onShelf, rev, tries

vars == <<delivery, onShelf, rev, tries>>

Typing ==
    /\ delivery \in [Deliveries -> [state : {"waiting", "reading", "shelved", "turned"},
                                    base : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ onShelf \subseteq Deliveries
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ tries \in [Deliveries -> 0..MaxRev]

Init ==
    /\ delivery = [d \in Deliveries |-> [state |-> "waiting", base |-> 0]]
    /\ onShelf = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ tries = [d \in Deliveries |-> 0]

\* A porter reads how full the controlled-drugs cupboard is, together with the
\* revision stamped on the count, and then walks the delivery over.  Porters
\* are slow but never give up: that walk can take arbitrarily long.
Read(d) ==
    /\ delivery[d].state = "waiting"
    /\ tries[d] < MaxRev
    /\ delivery' = [delivery EXCEPT ![d] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rev]]
    /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![d] = tries[d] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, rev>>

\* Putting the delivery away only lands while the revision the porter read is
\* still the one on the count, so a delivery that another porter shelved in
\* the meantime cannot be shelved on top of a count that has moved.
Shelve(d) ==
    /\ delivery[d].state = "reading"
    /\ delivery[d].base = rev
    /\ Cardinality(onShelf) < Cap
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ onShelf' = onShelf \cup {d}
    /\ delivery' = [delivery EXCEPT ![d].state = "shelved"]
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED tries

\* A porter whose read has gone stale walks back and reads again.
Restart(d) ==
    /\ delivery[d].state = "reading"
    /\ delivery[d].base # rev
    /\ tries[d] < MaxRev
    /\ delivery' = [delivery EXCEPT ![d].state = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, rev, tries>>

\* A delivery that cannot be put away -- the cupboard is full, or the porter
\* has used up their attempts -- is turned away to the ward safe instead.
TurnAway(d) ==
    /\ delivery[d].state \in {"waiting", "reading"}
    /\ \/ Cardinality(onShelf) = Cap
       \/ tries[d] = MaxRev
       \/ rev = MaxRev
    /\ delivery' = [delivery EXCEPT ![d].state = "turned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, rev, tries>>

Shut ==
    /\ \A d \in Deliveries : delivery[d].state \in {"shelved", "turned"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Deliveries : Read(d) \/ Shelve(d) \/ Restart(d) \/ TurnAway(d)
    \/ Shut

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Deliveries : Read(d))
    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Deliveries : Restart(d))
    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Deliveries : Shelve(d))
    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Deliveries : TurnAway(d))

\* Whenever anything is standing in the controlled-drugs cupboard, the cupboard
\* is holding no more than it is licensed for, however many porters raced each
\* other to put a delivery away.
CapacityRespected ==
    \A d \in Deliveries :
        (delivery[d].state = "shelved") => (Cardinality(onShelf) <= Cap)

EveryDeliveryEventuallySettles ==
    \A d \in Deliveries :
        (delivery[d].state = "waiting") ~>
            (delivery[d].state = "shelved" \/ delivery[d].state = "turned")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Deliveries = {delMorphine, delKetamine, delDiazepam}
    Cap = 2
    MaxRev = 3

INVARIANT CapacityRespected
PROPERTY EveryDeliveryEventuallySettles
nl:
A hospital pharmacy takes controlled-drug deliveries into a cupboard that is licensed to hold only so many packages at once. Exceeding that licensed capacity is a reportable breach, so the count must never go over it, however many porters are working at the same time.

The count is kept optimistically rather than under a lock. A porter reads how full the cupboard is, together with the revision stamped on the count, and then walks the delivery over. Porters here are slow but never give up: that walk can take arbitrarily long, and while it is happening another porter may have put a delivery away and moved the count on.

Putting a delivery away only lands while the revision the porter read is still the one stamped on the count, and landing bumps the revision. A porter whose read has gone stale walks back and reads afresh; each porter has only so many attempts in them. A delivery that cannot be put away -- because the cupboard is at its licensed limit, or the porter has used up their attempts, or the count has been stamped for the last time that shift -- is turned away and sent to the ward safe instead. Once every delivery has either been shelved or turned away the cupboard is shut.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever anything is standing in the controlled-drugs cupboard, the cupboard is holding no more than it is licensed for, however many porters raced each other to put a delivery away.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every waiting delivery eventually settles, either shelved in the cupboard or turned away to the ward safe.

---- MODULE W4Od1m0p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, MaxRev, MaxTry

Stamps == [flt : Flights, rev : 1..MaxRev]

VARIABLES clearance, tape, rev, tries

vars == <<clearance, tape, rev, tries>>

Typing ==
    /\ clearance \in [Flights -> [state : {"pending", "reading", "issued", "shelved"},
                                  base : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ tape \subseteq Stamps
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ tries \in [Flights -> 0..MaxTry]

Init ==
    /\ clearance = [f \in Flights |-> [state |-> "pending", base |-> 0]]
    /\ tape = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ tries = [f \in Flights |-> 0]

\* A controller reads the sequence board and the revision stamped on it, then
\* works the clearance up.  Controllers here are slow but never fail: that can
\* take arbitrarily long, and the board may move on underneath them.
Read(f) ==
    /\ clearance[f].state = "pending"
    /\ tries[f] < MaxTry
    /\ clearance' = [clearance EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rev]]
    /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![f] = tries[f] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tape, rev>>

\* Transmitting the clearance is irreversible: it goes out over the air and
\* onto the recorded tape, where it cannot be taken back.  It therefore only
\* goes out while the revision the controller read is still the board's, which
\* is what stops a second transmission being worked up against a stale read.
Transmit(f) ==
    /\ clearance[f].state = "reading"
    /\ clearance[f].base = rev
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ tape' = tape \cup {[flt |-> f, rev |-> rev + 1]}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ clearance' = [clearance EXCEPT ![f].state = "issued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED tries

\* A controller whose read has gone stale tears the strip up and starts again.
Retry(f) ==
    /\ clearance[f].state = "reading"
    /\ clearance[f].base # rev
    /\ tries[f] < MaxTry
    /\ clearance' = [clearance EXCEPT ![f].state = "pending"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tape, rev, tries>>

\* A flight that has run out of attempts, or that is still working when the
\* board is stamped out, is shelved to the next sequence rather than pushed.
Shelve(f) ==
    /\ clearance[f].state \in {"pending", "reading"}
    /\ \/ tries[f] = MaxTry
       \/ rev = MaxRev
    /\ clearance' = [clearance EXCEPT ![f].state = "shelved"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tape, rev, tries>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A f \in Flights : clearance[f].state \in {"issued", "shelved"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Read(f) \/ Transmit(f) \/ Retry(f) \/ Shelve(f)
    \/ Quiet

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A flight that has been cleared appears exactly once on the recorded tape,
\* however many times its strip was worked up and torn out again.
ClearanceTransmittedOnce ==
    \A f \in Flights :
        (clearance[f].state = "issued") =>
            (Cardinality({x \in tape : x.flt = f}) = 1)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Flights = {fltNorth, fltSouth, fltEast}
    MaxRev = 3
    MaxTry = 2

INVARIANT ClearanceTransmittedOnce
nl:
An airport tower works its departure sequence off a shared sequence board rather than under a lock, because the board is read far more often than it is written. A controller reads the board together with the revision stamped on it, and then works the clearance up on a strip.

Controllers here are slow but never fail. Working a clearance up can take arbitrarily long, and while it is happening another controller may transmit and move the board's revision on underneath the first one's read.

Transmitting a clearance is the irreversible step. It goes out over the air to the crew and onto the recorded tape, where it cannot be taken back or amended. A clearance therefore only goes out while the revision the controller read is still the board's standing revision, and transmitting stamps the tape and bumps that revision. That check is what stops a second transmission for the same flight being worked up against a stale read and going out on top of one that has already been recorded.

A controller whose read has gone stale tears the strip up and starts again, and each flight only gets so many attempts. A flight that has run out of attempts, or that is still being worked when the board is stamped for the last time in the sequence, is shelved to the next sequence rather than pushed out.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A flight that has been cleared appears exactly once on the recorded tape, however many times its strip was worked up and torn out again.
